data.title: Gov-copy sub-agent for empathetic, plain-language UI copy

content.text: ## Context

Government services teams using DSO ship UI copy ad-hoc through feature-developing agents and developers. The result is inconsistent voice, varying empathy, and copy that often fails federal plain-language standards — citizens completing benefits applications, claims, and tax filings encounter confusing questions, jargon-laden instructions, and error messages that don't tell them what to do next. Hard-coding strings in UI compounds the problem: it blocks future localization, hides cross-page voice drift, and makes copy quality dependent on per-PR review discipline. The worst failure mode is silent — copy that ships and confuses users, violating HCD principles, with no failing test to flag it. The Plain Writing Act of 2010 makes plain language a legal requirement for federal agencies; USWDS, GOV.UK, VA.gov, and 18F publish detailed style canons addressing exactly this problem. None are currently encoded in any DSO sub-agent.
## Success Criteria

- For any DSO epic touching UI copy, /dso:brainstorm tags the epic copy-needed and writes a `## Copy Needs` section conforming to the schema at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/copy-needs-section.md; each item carries stable_id, type, location, page (controlled identifier), validation rule.

- Any epic carrying the copy-needed tag produces a dedicated copy story when /dso:preplanning runs — auto-created by the story-decomposer sub-agent and populated from Copy Needs. When distinct(page) > 1, the story includes a coordination-pass task.

- When dispatched in a copy story, the gov-copy-writer sub-agent (model: sonnet) produces a YAML copy artifact conforming to the schema at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/gov-copy-artifact.md at the project-configured location (copy/<epic-id>.yaml default; overridable via copy.artifact_dir in dso-config.conf; absolute paths and `..` segments rejected).

- The produced copy artifact's items each carry: values: { label, hint, errors{} }; structured rationale: { rule_ids[], conflicts[], deviations[{rule_id, reason}] }; checks: { fk_grade, banned_words_found, active_voice } computed by deterministic post-processing (NOT LLM self-attestation).
- Coordination-pass receives the full first-pass rationale. Items whose rationale.rule_ids cites a hard-constraint canon rule (errors, validation, legal disclosures) cannot be mutated.

- The federal style canon — rules from USWDS forms, GOV.UK error/form patterns, VA.gov error anatomy, 18F content guide, Federal Plain Language Guidelines, and CDC reading-level guidance — ships as entries in the reference library corpus (epic 0b7c-d811), retrievable via ref-query.sh; gov-copy-writer loads relevant entries top-K by relevance (K ≤ 20) on dispatch and applies the documented precedence ladder (canon-rule > Copy Needs constraint > Users archetype > design-notes voice).

- Per-item closing condition: fk_grade ≤ 8, banned_words_found empty, active_voice = true for ≥ 95% of items in the produced artifact. Items below threshold are flagged in rationale.deviations with documented reason.

- Synthetic dogfood closing-session validation: run gov-copy-writer against a representative bad-copy example with intentionally jargon-laden questions, blame-language errors, and vague hints; before/after acceptance bar — average fk_grade decreases by ≥ 1 grade level, active_voice rate increases by ≥ 20 percentage points, banned_words_found count drops to 0.
## Dependencies

Depends on epic 0b7c-d811 (Add searchable UI/UX design knowledge base as a reference library) — provides the corpus schema, ref-query.sh retrieval contract with top-K + relevance scoring, and the canon-entry storage. 0b7c-d811's priority is raised to P0 as part of this epic's bookkeeping, and an SC is added to 0b7c-d811 requiring the federal-style-canon entries to be included.

Relates to: aaa1-7100 (Brainstorm UX understanding loop — same Phase 1.5 surface; future brainstorm coordinates with the copy-needed probe established here), 1048-67d0 (Preplanning UX reference injection — same story-decomposer surface), jira-dig-2569 (Add a Cleanup Story for every epic during preplanning — shared auto-created-story pattern).
## Approach

Add a sonnet-tier gov-copy-writer sub-agent that loads federal-style-canon entries from epic 0b7c-d811's reference library via ref-query.sh (top-K by relevance, K ≤ 20) with a documented canon-source precedence ladder, structured rationale schema, and deterministic post-processing for the checks block (no LLM self-attestation). Brainstorm Phase 1.5 detects UI-copy needs and tags the epic plus writes a formally-schema'd Copy Needs section; preplanning's story-decomposer auto-creates the copy story; multi-page stories include a conditional coordination-pass that respects hard-constraint canon rules.
## State Lifecycle
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
| copy-needed epic tag | /dso:brainstorm Phase 1.5 when copy needs detected | n/a (additive) | /dso:preplanning story-decomposer | n/a — durable; persists with the epic |

| copy.artifact_dir config key | /dso:onboarding per consuming project (optional; default copy/) | Operator edit | /dso:sprint task-dispatch passes path to gov-copy-writer | When consuming project is decommissioned |

| Copy artifact `<copy_dir>/<epic-id>.yaml` | gov-copy-writer first-pass dispatch | gov-copy-writer coordination-pass (multi-page only) | Implementation-story application code | Manual deletion when epic reverted |

| Federal style canon entries (in 0b7c-d811's corpus) | This epic's implementation stories | Author edits with prior-art citation | gov-copy-writer via ref-query.sh | Edits via reference-library corpus management |
## Scenario Analysis
- runtime: ref-query.sh empty or partial returns (high), coordination-pass race on artifact file (high), concurrent copy stories collide on epic-id filename (medium)
- deployment: copy.artifact_dir conflicts with .gitignore or existing project directories (high), brainstorm Phase 1.5 tag-write race with concurrent epic-description edits (high)

- configuration: Copy Needs items with missing validation rule or page fields produce schema-conforming but unusable artifacts (high), banned-words and fk_grade thresholds not configurable per agency context (medium)

- assumption: Phase 1.5 UI-copy detection precision and recall (high), story-decomposer reliably parses Copy Needs format (high), single sonnet agent satisfies all six style canons without conflict (high), plain-language compliance checkable via fk_grade plus banned_words plus active_voice (high), canon entries stable over time vs source-cadence updates (medium), coordination-pass converges in one re-dispatch (medium)
## Prompt Alignment Findings

Matched LLM-instruction signals: skill file modifications, agent definitions, prompt templates. Bot-psychologist behavioral findings adopted into the approach: (1) deterministic checks (not LLM self-attestation); (2) explicit canon-source precedence ladder; (3) structured rationale schema with rule_ids, conflicts, deviations; (4) formal Copy Needs schema with controlled page identifier; (5) top-K canon-entry cap (K ≤ 20); (6) coordination-pass receives full first-pass rationale, hard-constraint items immutable.
### Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered — user-requested at session start (prior-art research on GitHub for plain-language copy agents); findings incorporated into Approach. Bright-line conditions that fired: user-request trigger; novel architectural pattern (corpus-loaded LLM-agent canon).
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered — 13 of 17 red-team scenarios survived blue-team filter; 4 filtered as mitigated by spec revisions or explicitly out of scope.
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: none — Value reviewer passed on cycle 1 after spec remediation incorporating bot-psychologist findings.
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered.
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered (no external integration signals; ref-query.sh is an in-plugin dependency).
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keyword: skill file modifications (also agent definitions, prompt templates).
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable (per-story dispatch, no volume-sensitive decision).

- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): skipped — user override (timeout authorization). Manual triage applied during the dialogue identified overlap with 0b7c-d811 (resolved via depends_on with priority bump), aaa1-7100 (relates_to), 1048-67d0 (relates_to), jira-dig-2569 (relates_to).
## Closure Checks
- Dogfood validation harness produces PASS verdict (acceptance bar met) — bash plugins/dso/scripts/dogfood-gov-copy.sh exits 0.
